subject: Intermittent connection-affinity causing token desync during demo: field triage and workaround
messages:
From: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acme.com>
To: irene_choi@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: logan_wright@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 20 May 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Demo glitch - tokens misaligned after reconnect (recording attached)

Hi Irene / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo this morning. We saw a repeatable issue where the demo app (client using the SDK) loses alignment after the client-side reconnect: the response stream starts at an earlier token index and the UI shows duplicated content. Attaching the small recording and the client trace. This happened twice during a 15-minute session.

What we observed:
- Start session: request A (prefetch enabled) -> normal streaming.
- Mid-session: network hiccup (simulated) -> SDK reconnects, resumes.
- After reconnect: server response starts from token ~-8 relative to last shown token, so UI re-renders a chunk.

This breaks the demo narrative. Can this be patched quickly or is there a recommended mitigation (config toggle) we can flip from our side?

Attachments: connection-trace-20290520.log (text/plain), recording-demo-20290520.mp4 (note: large)

Thanks,
Sarah
Head of Product

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear repro and trace. Looping in Runtime (Dev) and Sales Eng (Logan) to triage.

Initial read: it looks like a reconnect path where the client rehydrates the KV cache but the server-side stream starts with a slightly different token offset. Two immediate asks from us:
1) Dev: can you confirm whether reconnects can emit overlapping token ranges when prefetch + session-affinity toggles are in play?
2) SE/Product: short-term workaround for Acme to avoid duplicate rendering during demos (config or client-side debounce).

I'll attach the trace to the ticket (INF-8421).

Irene Choi

Subject: Re: Demo glitch - tokens misaligned after reconnect (recording attached)

Thanks for the ping and trace — dug into the log. Quick summary:
- The runtime accepts the resume request and attempts to replay the KV cache state. Because prefetch was enabled on the client, there are two streams of in-flight tokens (prefetched + live). If the reconnection completes while prefetched tokens are still buffered client-side, the server-side stream will re-emit a small window (typically 6-12 tokens) to ensure model context consistency.
- The implementation currently lacks a short de-duplication handshake for session resumes (we assumed clients would dedupe on client id + offset).

Short-term mitigation (can be pushed as a minor SDK patch or config flip):
- Server-side: we can enable a resume-handshake flag that requires the client to include its last-acknowledged-token-index. The runtime will then suppress re-emitting tokens <= that index. Patch risk: low, but requires tiny runtime change + SDK bump to set the header on resume.
- Client-side workaround: debounce rendering for N=12 tokens after a resume event (SE recommended for demos).

I can prototype the server flag in a branch and provide a repro script (repro-script.zip) — low-risk, targets next-week patch window. For the immediate demo, recommend the client debounce + temporarily disable prefetch for Acme demo runs.

Action items:
- Dev to attach repro branch and instructions (Irene: will drop into Drive).
- SE (Logan) to coordinate with Acme to toggle prefetch and try the debounce approach for the next demo.
- Product (Marissa/Soojin) to weigh in on making the resume-handshake a roadmap prioritization item if we see more field hits.

Dev Patel
Senior Runtime Engineer, Redwood Inference
[attachment: repro-script.zip (application/zip)]
From: logan_wright@redwood.ai

Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 22 May 2029 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Demo glitch - tokens misaligned after reconnect (recording attached)

Sarah — thanks for reporting this and for the recording. We're going to run the quick mitigations for your next demo on Thursday:

1) Quick demo config (today): Disable client prefetch in your demo build (we'll send a patched demo artifact). This should prevent the overlapping in-flight token windows.
2) Immediate client guidance: Add a small render-debounce of 12 tokens after any reconnect event. That avoids visible duplication without altering model outputs.
3) Short-term fix (engineering): Dev will ship the resume-handshake flag in a runtime patch early next week. We'll provide a small SDK update that sets the last-ack header on reconnect.

I'll coordinate the patched demo artifact and the toggles with you (Sarah) today — can you confirm a 10am PT slot tomorrow for a quick smoke test?

Thanks — appreciate the patience. We'll keep this from interrupting your exec demo.

— Logan Wright
Principal Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
